analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) causes hand, foot, and mouth disease and can trigger life-threatening neurological complications, yet the sequence-level physicochemical correlates of CNS involvement across globally circulating lineages remain incompletely defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here we screened 15,247 EV-A71 genomic entries spanning 1998-2024, retaining 267 full-length sequences (≥7,000 bp) with confirmed clinical outcomes (7 central nervous system [CNS]-involved, 260 non-CNS).
analysis.methods: Each polyprotein position was encoded by three Z-scale descriptors-hydrophobicity (Z1), molecular volume (Z2), and electrostatic polarity (Z3)-converting discrete residue identities into a continuous biophysical feature space. A two-stage statistical pipeline (Mann-Whitney U screening followed by odds-ratio ranking) distilled 20 significant loci down to five core positions. Leave-one-out cross-validated logistic regression achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.889) among eight algorithms benchmarked.
analysis.main_results: SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) assigned the largest model contribution to P2124_Z1 (OR = 4.28; 95% CI 1.47-12.51), while P1246_Z3 was statistically associated with lower CNS odds (OR = 0.50).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Reference-strain mapping linked the five polyprotein coordinates to mature-protein residues in 3D RdRp, 3C protease, 2C helicase, and 2A, thereby providing structural context for cautious biochemical hypotheses rather than confirmed mechanisms. The study presents the five-position physicochemical signature and nomogram as hypothesis-generating tools for prioritising candidate neurovirulence markers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a framework for prioritising candidate neurovirulence markers, which could inform surveillance and early detection of high-risk EV-A71 strains. The identified physicochemical signature may guide future studies on pathogenesis and therapeutic targeting.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This extreme 7:260 class imbalance, reflecting the scarcity of publicly available full-length CNS-associated EV-A71 genomes, is the principal limitation and interpretive premise of the study. Because the AUC is estimated from only seven positive samples, it should be regarded as an exploratory internal performance signal rather than definitive evidence of generalisable accuracy, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the physicochemical determinants of EV-A71 neurovirulence by analyzing 267 full-length genomes (7 CNS-involved, 260 non-CNS) from 1998-2024. Using machine learning and structural analysis, researchers identified five key polyprotein positions (P2124_Z1, P997_Z2, P1246_Z3, P1743_Z2, P1711_Z1) significantly associated with CNS involvement. The model achieved an AUC of 0.889, though limited by the small number of CNS genomes. The findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing neurovirulence markers, requiring validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

analysis.scope_and_question: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a major causative agent of hand, foot, and mouth disease, yet no specific antiviral therapy has been approved.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This study systematically evaluated the efficacy and mechanisms of alkaloids against EV-A71 infection by integrating meta-analysis, network pharmacology, and molecular docking. Nine animal studies were included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Meta-analysis suggested that alkaloid intervention significantly improved survival (OR = 30.62, 95% CI: 10.44–89.82), reduced clinical severity, attenuated body weight loss, and decreased viral loads in infected tissues. Network pharmacology predicted 155 shared targets between seven active alkaloids and EV-A71-related genes, with MAPK1, MAPK3, JUN, AURKB, and MAPK8 recognized as core targets. Functional enrichment analysis suggested significant involvement of the MAPK, TNF, and IL-17 signaling pathways. Molecular docking provided computational support for stable binding affinities between active alkaloids and core targets (−6.7 to −9.3 kcal/mol).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Subgroup analyses preliminarily suggested that quinolizidine alkaloids and high-dose regimens (>5 mg/kg) may be associated with preclinical intervention effects.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings support the potential of alkaloids as candidates for the development of novel anti-EV-A71 therapeutics.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and mechanisms of alkaloids against Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), a major cause of hand, foot, and mouth disease with no approved specific therapy. Integrating meta-analysis, network pharmacology, and molecular docking, the study included nine animal studies. Results showed alkaloid intervention significantly improved survival (OR = 30.62), reduced clinical severity, attenuated weight loss, and decreased viral loads. Network pharmacology identified 155 shared targets, with MAPK1, MAPK3, JUN, AURKB, and MAPK8 as core targets, and highlighted involvement of MAPK, TNF, and IL-17 pathways. Molecular docking confirmed stable binding affinities (−6.7 to −9.3 kcal/mol). Subgroup analyses suggested quinolizidine alkaloids and high-dose regimens (>5 mg/kg) may be particularly effective. The findings support alkaloids as promising candidates for novel anti-EV-A71 therapeutics through direct antiviral and host-directed mechanisms.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the molecular mechanism by which enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) invades respiratory cells, focusing on the newly identified receptor MFSD6 and its role in viral entry.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed near-atomic-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) to analyze historical and contemporary AFM-associated EV-D68 strains and their complexes with the third extracellular loop of MFSD6 (MFSD6-L3).
analysis.methods: Structural analyses were conducted to determine the virus-receptor engagement mechanism, followed by functional analyses to define the contributions of receptor-contacting residues and glycans to viral attachment and entry.
analysis.main_results: The study revealed a previously unrecognized 'binary gating switch' mechanism where the N200-V208 segment of MFSD6 inserts into one capsomer, while its sialyl-Gal-terminated glycan engages an adjacent capsomer, with Neu5Ac binding inducing conformational rearrangements that prime infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as refining the molecular basis of EV-D68 recognition of MFSD6 and revealing a glycan-mediated dual-lock mechanism that enhances receptor specificity and ensures productive infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide broader insight into enterovirus tropism and establish a framework for structure-guided antiviral design, potentially informing strategies to prevent EV-D68 infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high due to the use of near-atomic-resolution cryo-EM and functional analyses, though limitations may include the specificity of the findings to EV-D68 and potential generalizability to other enteroviruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) uses the respiratory receptor MFSD6 to enter cells, revealing a novel 'binary gating switch' mechanism. Through near-atomic-resolution cryo-electron microscopy, the researchers discovered that EV-D68 engages MFSD6 via two distinct interactions: a protein segment insertion and glycan binding. This dual-receptor checkpoint mechanism primes the virus for infection by inducing conformational changes that destabilize the virion. The findings enhance our understanding of enterovirus tropism and provide a foundation for developing targeted antiviral therapies against EV-D68, a virus causing severe respiratory disease and poliomyelitis-like illness in children.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The development of animal models infected with Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) is limited by insufficient neurovirulence, which hinders the study of pathogenesis mechanisms and antiviral drug evaluation. The lack of animal models that reliably recapitulate the neurological manifestations of Coxsackievirus A16 infection has constrained progress in understanding CVA16 neuropathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We aimed to develop a neonatal ICR mouse model for CVA16 infection, wherein infected brain tissue was continuously passaged from 2-day-old ICR suckling mice, resulting in a highly neurovirulent mouse-adapted strain (CVA16-P5) to establish optimal infection conditions for antiviral assessment. By systematically optimizing viral dose, inoculation route, and age at infection, we defined conditions that reproducibly induced progressive neurological disease and multisystem involvement.
analysis.methods: Whole-genome sequencing identified a nonsynonymous mutation in the VP1 capsid protein associated with enhanced neurovirulence during mouse adaptation. Transcriptomic analysis of neural tissues revealed tissue-specific interferon-dominated immune responses and signatures of systemic viral dissemination that recapitulate key features of severe human infection.
analysis.main_results: Infection with the CVA16-P5 strain resulted in consistent pathological alterations across multiple tissues, accompanied by characteristic neurological manifestations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The CVA16-P5-adapted strain infection model provides a robust experimental platform for investigating CVA16 pathogenesis and for the preclinical evaluation of vaccines and antiviral drugs against neurotropic enteroviruses. This model enables the analysis of tissue-specific immune responses, viral dissemination, and genetic determinants of neurovirulence, including a VP1 mutation associated with enhanced pathogenicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: By providing a reproducible and physiologically relevant system for studying severe CVA16 infection, the CVA16-P5-adapted strain infection model setup in this study supports mechanistic studies of CVA16 pathogenesis and facilitates the preclinical evaluation of vaccines and antiviral drugs against neurotropic enteroviruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high as the study provides a well-characterized mouse model with reproducible neurological disease and molecular insights into neurovirulence.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a neonatal ICR mouse model for Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) infection by passaging virus in brain tissue to create a highly neurovirulent strain (CVA16-P5). The model reproducibly induces progressive neurological disease and multisystem pathology, with transcriptomic analysis revealing tissue-specific interferon-dominated immune responses and systemic viral dissemination. Whole-genome sequencing identified a VP1 capsid protein mutation associated with enhanced neurovirulence. This robust experimental platform enables mechanistic studies of CVA16 pathogenesis and preclinical evaluation of vaccines and antiviral drugs against neurotropic enteroviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common pediatric infectious disease that frequently causes outbreaks in the Asia-Pacific region. The lack of cross-protection among serotypes highlights the need for multivalent vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Epidemiologic data and clinical specimens were collected from reported HFMD cases in Xi'an between 2020 and 2024. Among 2596 specimens, 2148 (82.7%) were enterovirus-positive.
analysis.methods: Pan-enterovirus, enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16), coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6), and coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) were detected by real-time polymerase chain reaction. The VP1 regions of CVA6 and CVA16 were amplified, sequenced, and phylogenetically analyzed.
analysis.main_results: The proportions of detected viruses were: CVA6 52.8%, CVA16 23.8%, CVA10 5.0%, and EV-A71 0.3%. CVA6 predominated in 2020, 2022, and 2023, while CVA16 predominated in 2021 and 2024. Compared with CVA16 infection, CVA6 infection was associated with younger age (3.25 vs. 4.14 years, P < 0.001) and a higher risk of severe disease (OR = 12.93).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: CVA6 and CVA16 are the predominant HFMD pathogens in Xi'an with alternating circulation. All identified CVA6 strains belonged to the D3a subtype, whereas the B1a subtype predominated among CVA16 strains.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The first emergence of the CVA16 B1c sublineage in 2024 mirrors national trends and warrants intensified surveillance. The findings provide insights into the changing epidemiology of HFMD pathogens, which can inform vaccine development and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on reported HFMD cases and clinical specimens, which may not capture all circulating strains. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational data and does not include experimental controls.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the pathogenic surveillance and genetic characteristics of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) pathogens in Xi'an from 2020 to 2024. It identifies that coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6) and coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16) are the predominant pathogens, with alternating circulation over the study period. CVA6 was associated with younger age and a higher risk of severe disease. All CVA6 strains were classified as subgenotype D3a, while CVA16 strains were categorized into B1a, B1b, and B1c subtypes, with B1a being the most prevalent. The emergence of the B1c lineage in 2024 is noted as a significant trend. The study highlights the need for intensified surveillance and the potential for multivalent vaccines due to the lack of cross-protection among serotypes. However, the findings are based on observational data and may not fully account for all circulating strains, limiting the strength of the evidence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report a rare case of chronic enteroviral encephalitis developing in a patient undergoing rituximab maintenance therapy for follicular lymphoma, highlighting the risk of severe enteroviral complications in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a 29-year-old woman with stage IV, grade 3A follicular lymphoma who developed chronic enteroviral encephalitis during rituximab maintenance therapy after achieving complete remission with R-CHOP.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic evaluation included cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR to confirm enterovirus infection.
analysis.main_results: The patient presented with confusion and involuntary movements shortly after the sixth rituximab maintenance dose, and cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR confirmed enterovirus infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret chronic enteroviral encephalitis as a rare but serious complication in immunocompromised patients, particularly those receiving B-cell-depleting therapies like rituximab.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings emphasize the need for heightened awareness and monitoring of enteroviral infections in patients on anti-CD20 therapies to prevent severe neurological complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited by the case report design, which lacks a control group and cannot establish causality, though the diagnostic confirmation provides moderate confidence in the reported association.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 29-year-old woman with stage IV, grade 3A follicular lymphoma who developed chronic enteroviral encephalitis during rituximab maintenance therapy. After achieving complete remission with six cycles of R-CHOP, she received rituximab every three months and presented with confusion and involuntary movements after the sixth dose. Cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR confirmed enterovirus infection. The authors highlight that chronic enteroviral encephalitis is a rare but serious complication in immunocompromised patients, particularly those receiving B-cell-depleting therapies. The findings underscore the importance of monitoring for enteroviral infections in such patients to prevent severe neurological outcomes.

Most HFMD cases are mild and can be managed at home with proper care. The public was advised on hand hygiene, food safety, proper disinfection, and vaccination to reduce risks. The CDC emphasized ongoing surveillance and urged parents to ensure children follow preventive measures to maintain a safe and healthy summer.

analysis.brief_en: Heilongjiang Province has issued four key health recommendations to prevent enterovirus infections like norovirus and hand-foot-mouth disease during the summer season. Director Bao Mingjia from the provincial CDC emphasizes hand hygiene, food and water safety, monitoring of patient symptoms, and respiratory disease prevention. Specific measures include proper handwashing, thorough cleaning of fruits and vegetables, separating raw and cooked food, and regular ventilation. The CDC notes that while the overall situation remains stable, continued vigilance is needed. Parents are advised to seek immediate medical attention for children with persistent high fever, lethargy, or frequent vomiting.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a major cause of hand-foot-mouth disease in children, and there are currently no specific antiviral drugs available for its prevention or treatment. The study aimed to address this unmet need by systematically characterizing the antiviral efficacy and mechanism of action of IMB-A3, a compound previously shown to exhibit anti-EV-A71 activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the in vitro and in vivo antiviral efficacy of IMB-A3 and investigated its mechanism of action. It included experiments in infected cells and mice muscles, as well as lethal EV-A71 infection models in mice.
analysis.methods: The study assessed the effects of IMB-A3 on EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA levels in infected cells and mice muscles. Mechanism studies evaluated the direct interaction between IMB-A3 and the EV-A71 2C protein, its impact on 2C protein activities, and its role in promoting CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of the 2C protein.
analysis.main_results: IMB-A3 treatment reduced EV-A71 VP1 protein and viral RNA levels in infected cells and mice muscles. In vivo, IMB-A3 effectively protected mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. Mechanistically, IMB-A3 facilitated the interaction between 2C and CRBN, promoting ubiquitination and degradation of the N-terminal region of the 2C protein.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that IMB-A3 acts as a molecular glue degrader of the EV-A71 2C protein, providing a mechanistic basis for its antiviral activity. This represents a novel approach to targeting EV-A71 by inducing targeted protein degradation rather than inhibiting enzymatic function.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies IMB-A3 as a promising candidate for the development of targeted antiviral therapies against EV-A71, potentially addressing the current lack of specific treatments. Its mechanism of action suggests broader applicability for designing degraders of viral proteins.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro and mouse models, which may not fully recapitulate human infection dynamics or safety profiles. While the mechanism is well-characterized, further studies are needed to evaluate efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and safety in humans before clinical translation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated IMB-A3, an isoindolinone derivative, as a potential antiviral against enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), a leading cause of hand-foot-mouth disease in children for which no specific treatments exist. The research systematically evaluated IMB-A3's antiviral efficacy in vitro and in vivo, demonstrating its ability to reduce viral protein and RNA levels in infected cells and protect mice from lethal EV-A71 infection. Mechanistic analyses revealed that IMB-A3 functions as a molecular glue, facilitating CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of the EV-A71 2C protein without inhibiting its ATPase or helicase activities. This targeted protein degradation approach represents a novel strategy for antiviral development. The findings highlight IMB-A3's potential as a lead compound for future drug design, though the current evidence is confined to preclinical models and requires validation in human studies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the evolutionary and molecular characteristics of high-Shannon entropy codons in the VP1 protein of Coxsackievirus A6, addressing the need to understand how these codons may contribute to immune evasion and viral adaptation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed global genomic data of Coxsackievirus A6, focusing on the spatiotemporal dynamics of specific codon replacements and their potential impact on viral structure and function.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed direct-coupling analysis to examine residue pair co-evolution and conducted spatiotemporal analysis to track the global replacement of 283A with 283T after 2017, as well as the localized circulation of minor variants.
analysis.main_results: A spatiotemporal analysis showed that 283A replaced 283T on a global scale after 2017, while minor variants (e.g. 30D, 97I, 174A) exhibited localized circulation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings highlight the predominance of high-entropy codons in VP1 surface loops (BC, DE, EF and HI), suggesting ongoing adaptive selection pressure that may influence the virus's ability to evade immune responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Continuous genomic surveillance is imperative for tracking emerging variants (e.g. 283V, 97N) and for informing vaccine design against evolving CVA6 strains.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on global genomic data, which may not capture all regional variations, and the absence of direct functional validation of the observed structural changes.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the evolutionary and molecular features of high-Shannon entropy codons in the VP1 protein of Coxsackievirus A6, focusing on their potential role in immune evasion and structural adaptation. Using direct-coupling analysis and spatiotemporal genomic data, the researchers identified the global replacement of 283A with 283T after 2017 and the localized circulation of minor variants such as 30D, 97I, and 174A. The findings suggest that high-entropy codons in VP1 surface loops are under adaptive selection pressure, which could impact the virus's ability to evade immune responses. The study emphasizes the importance of genomic surveillance to monitor emerging variants and guide vaccine development. However, the analysis is limited by its reliance on existing genomic data without direct functional validation of the observed structural changes. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of experimental confirmation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) causes acute respiratory illnesses and has been implicated in acute flaccid myelitis, but the dynamics of EV-D68 neutralizing antibodies in adults remain poorly characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated EV-D68 neutralizing antibody levels in retail workers (≥18 years) in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic, using paired serum samples (N=194) collected 48 weeks apart between June 2021 and October 2022.
analysis.methods: Neutralizing antibodies were measured in paired serum samples from retail workers enrolled in a prospective SARS-CoV-2 cohort at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Québec-Université Laval, using microneutralization assays.
analysis.main_results: EV-D68 neutralizing antibody seroprevalence was high (>85%), with the vast majority of participants (97%) showing stable or reduced titers over 48 weeks, resulting in a statistically significant overall reduction in geometric mean titer (GMT), p<0.001; however, 6/194 (3%) participants had a marked increase in titers (≥4-fold), with GMT rising from 21 (10-57) to 593 (57-7241).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the decline in neutralizing antibody titers in most participants as evidence of waning immunity, while the increase in a small subset suggested potential ongoing EV-D68 or other enterovirus circulation in Quebec following the lift of non-pharmaceutical interventions, consistent with documented EV-D68 resurgence in the United States during the same period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study complements pediatric data on EV-D68 immunity and highlights the importance of serological surveillance in adults to monitor immunity and inform public health responses to enterovirus resurgence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to retail workers in a single geographic region, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the prospective cohort design but with potential generalizability constraints to other populations or settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the dynamics of neutralizing antibodies against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) in adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. Researchers measured neutralizing antibody levels in paired serum samples from 194 retail workers in Canada, collected 48 weeks apart. The findings revealed high seroprevalence (>85%), with most participants showing stable or reduced titers over time, resulting in a significant overall decline in geometric mean titer (p<0.001). However, a small subset (3%) exhibited a marked increase in titers, suggesting potential ongoing EV-D68 circulation. The study complements pediatric data and underscores the importance of adult serological surveillance for enteroviruses, with moderate evidence strength due to the cohort design but limited generalizability.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Non-polio enteroviruses, particularly EV-D68 and EV-A71, have emerged as major pediatric threats due to their association with acute flaccid myelitis and high mortality. This study aims to develop an effective intranasal vaccine incorporating zymosan to protect against EV-D68 and EV-A71 infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated vaccine efficacy in a neonatal mouse model using inactivated EV-D68 vaccines and monovalent and bivalent intranasal vaccines with zymosan.
analysis.methods: We first prepared an inactivated EV-D68 vaccine to compare immunogenicity across administration routes. Next, we tested monovalent and bivalent intranasal vaccines with zymosan to assess multi-dose and adjuvant effects.
analysis.main_results: Two doses of inactivated EV-D68 with intranasal priming effectively induced mucosal and systemic immunity. A three-dose regimen further strengthened vaccine-specific immunity, with zymosan amplifying responses in both formulations and enhancing serum neutralization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that combining bivalent antigens with zymosan broadened and enhanced the intranasal vaccine efficacy, providing a promising approach for early-life protection against EV-A71 and EV-D68 infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings advance nasal spray vaccine strategies and offer a promising approach for early-life protection against EV-A71 and EV-D68 infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations. The evidence strength is high as the study demonstrates significant protection with zymosan-adjuvanted vaccines in a neonatal mouse model.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed an intranasal vaccine incorporating zymosan to protect against EV-D68 and EV-A71 infections in neonatal mice. The bivalent vaccine with zymosan adjuvant effectively induced mucosal and systemic immunity, with a three-dose regimen enhancing serum neutralization. Serum transfer from vaccinated donors provided significant protection against viral challenges, demonstrating the vaccine's efficacy. The findings offer a promising approach for early-life protection against these enteroviruses and advance nasal spray vaccine strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the associations between microbial infections and islet autoimmunity in children with genetic susceptibility to type 1 diabetes, building on previous evidence linking coxsackievirus B to the development of type 1 diabetes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nested case-control study within the TRIGR study was conducted, analyzing follow-up serum samples from 240 islet autoantibody-positive case children and 436 age- and country-matched control children.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were tested for IgG class antibodies against 10 respiratory and gastrointestinal microbes using an enzyme immunoassay, and for neutralizing antibodies against all six coxsackievirus B types.
analysis.main_results: Coxsackievirus B5 was associated with an increased risk of islet autoimmunity (OR 2.22, 95% CI 1.29–3.80, p = 0.004, corrected p = 0.024), with the association remaining after adjustment for HLA, sex, and maternal type 1 diabetes. The association was particularly observed for infections occurring more than 12 months (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.06–3.84, p = 0.032) and 0–6 months (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.11–6.35, p = 0.028) before the first detection of multiple islet autoantibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as supporting the role of coxsackievirus B infections in the pathogenesis of type 1 diabetes, particularly highlighting the timing of infections relative to the onset of islet autoimmunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that monitoring coxsackievirus B infections could be important for understanding the development of islet autoimmunity and type 1 diabetes in genetically susceptible children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its reliance on serum samples and the potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and adjustment for key variables.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between coxsackievirus B infections and islet autoimmunity in children with a genetic predisposition to type 1 diabetes. Using a nested case-control design within the TRIGR study, serum samples from 240 case children and 436 control children were analyzed for antibodies against 10 microbes and all six coxsackievirus B types. The results showed that coxsackievirus B5 was linked to an increased risk of islet autoimmunity, with the association persisting after adjusting for HLA, sex, and maternal diabetes. The risk was particularly notable for infections occurring more than 12 months or within 0–6 months before the first detection of multiple islet autoantibodies. These findings support the role of coxsackievirus B in the pathogenesis of type 1 diabetes and highlight the importance of timing in viral exposure. However, the study's reliance on serum samples and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in the results, though the evidence is considered strong due to the large sample size and statistical adjustments.

analysis.research_question_and_background: KREMEN1 serves as a cellular receptor for a major group of enteroviruses causing hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), including CVA2–CVA6, CVA8, CVA10, and CVA12, but the molecular determinants on the receptor side that govern broad enterovirus recognition remain incompletely understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used alanine scanning of 29 KREMEN1 residues at the CVA10–KRM1 interface and structural analysis to identify critical residues, and tested CRISPR-engineered mouse Krm1 W94A mutant mice for resistance to CVA10 infection.
analysis.methods: Alanine scanning of KREMEN1 residues was performed to assess their impact on CVA10 infection, and structural analysis was used to examine interactions between KRM1 W94 and viral VP2 K140.
analysis.main_results: Alanine scanning revealed that only W94A nearly abolished CVA10 infection, and structural analysis showed that KRM1 W94 engages in a π-cation interaction with the viral VP2 residue K140; CRISPR-engineered mouse Krm1 W94A mutant mice were fully resistant to CVA10 infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish KRM1 W94 as a critical receptor determinant that pairs with the universally conserved VP2 K140 to enable enterovirus infection, providing a structural and mechanistic basis for the broad recognition of KRM1-dependent enteroviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings offer insights that may guide the future development of broad-spectrum antiviral strategies against hand, foot, and mouth disease, which affects millions of children worldwide each year.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high, as the study includes both in vitro and in vivo results with structural analysis, but limitations may include the focus on a specific group of enteroviruses and the use of a mouse model.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies KREMEN1 tryptophan 94 (W94) as an essential residue for KRM1-mediated enterovirus infection. Alanine scanning revealed that W94A nearly abolished CVA10 infection, and structural analysis showed that KRM1 W94 engages in a π-cation interaction with the viral VP2 residue K140. CRISPR-engineered mouse Krm1 W94A mutant mice were fully resistant to CVA10 infection and all KRM1-dependent enteroviruses. These findings establish KRM1 W94 as a critical receptor determinant that pairs with the universally conserved VP2 K140, providing a structural and mechanistic basis for broad recognition of KRM1-dependent enteroviruses and offering insights for future broad-spectrum antiviral strategies against hand, foot, and mouth disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the rare manifestation of onychomadesis (nail shedding) as a delayed complication of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), focusing on the role of coxsackievirus A6 and A10 in disrupting nail matrix function and growth.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review article that synthesizes current knowledge on onychomadesis, its association with HFMD, and the viral mechanisms involved in nail matrix disruption.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a literature review summarizing the pathophysiology of onychomadesis, viral replication in the nail matrix, and the interference with Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathways.
analysis.main_results: The findings confirm that coxsackievirus A10 can disrupt nail growth by interfering with Wnt/β-catenin signaling, leading to temporary nail growth arrest and shedding, with spontaneous recovery within three to six months.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret onychomadesis as a rare but significant complication of HFMD, with novel insights into the viral interference of nail stem cell differentiation and proliferation pathways.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of recognizing onychomadesis as a post-infection complication to avoid unnecessary interventions and reassure parents during the recovery period.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study is a review article without primary data, but it provides a comprehensive synthesis of existing literature on the topic.

analysis.summary_en: This review article explores onychomadesis, a rare complication of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD), focusing on the role of coxsackievirus A6 and A10 in disrupting nail matrix function. The study highlights that viral replication in the nail matrix can cause temporary nail growth arrest and shedding, with spontaneous recovery within three to six months. The authors provide novel insights into how coxsackievirus A10 interferes with Wnt/β-catenin signaling, disrupting cell proliferation and nail stem cell differentiation. The findings emphasize the importance of recognizing onychomadesis as a post-infection manifestation to avoid unnecessary interventions and reassure parents. While the evidence is moderate due to the review nature of the study, it offers valuable guidance for healthcare professionals in managing this condition.

analysis.brief_en: This article provides comprehensive guidance on Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD), a common childhood illness caused primarily by Coxsackievirus A6, A16, and Enterovirus A71. It details symptoms such as fever, mouth ulcers, and rashes on hands and feet, which typically resolve within 2-3 days. The disease spreads through direct contact with infected secretions or contaminated objects, with childcare facilities being high-risk environments. While most cases are mild, severe complications like brainstem encephalitis can occur. No specific antiviral treatment exists, so management focuses on symptom relief and hydration. Prevention emphasizes proper handwashing, avoiding shared items, and cleaning surfaces. A vaccine is available for EV-A71 in young children to reduce severe complications.

analysis.time: Published Jul 30, 2026 12:00 PM EDT. Event timing: Late summer, with cases typically appearing after a respiratory illness or fever by a few days to a couple of weeks.
analysis.location_and_population: United States (49 states and the District of Columbia). Affected population: Previously healthy children.
analysis.event: Sudden arm or leg weakness in children, identified as acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare neurologic condition. CDC guidance: Suspect AFM in any child with acute flaccid limb weakness, particularly after a recent febrile or respiratory illness.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Rare condition; peak years (2014, 2016, 2018) reported 120 to 238 cases annually. Can progress quickly to breathing difficulty requiring intensive care. Risk escalation signs include neck weakness, facial droop, difficulty swallowing, or breathing changes.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC surveillance reports provide consistent guidance for clinicians. The frequency is reassuring, but the weakened link to enteroviruses is not established. Source limitation: Full original article body was reviewed.

analysis.brief_en: A rare but serious neurologic condition, acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), causes sudden limb weakness in children, typically following a respiratory illness. CDC urges parents and clinicians to recognize this as a medical emergency, especially when accompanied by symptoms like facial droop or breathing difficulties. While cases have been reported across the U.S., recent data shows lower frequency compared to previous peaks. The exact cause remains under investigation, though enteroviruses have been historically linked. Late summer is a critical period for vigilance, as this is when AFM cases have previously emerged.

analysis.time: Published on 2026-08-01. Event date: approximately one week prior to admission (patient presented with symptoms beginning about a week before admission).
analysis.location_and_population: Country not specified. Patient: 33-year-old immunocompetent woman with no significant past medical history, no immunosuppressive therapy, and no prior similar dermatologic episodes.
analysis.event: Probable Coxsackievirus infection in an immunocompetent adult presenting with severe vulvar ulcerations, oral ulcers, and a painful maculopapular rash on lower extremities that evolved into pustules, initially mimicking disseminated herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection and Behçet's disease. Reported in a Cureus medical case report.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Patient was afebrile and hemodynamically stable but demonstrated a marked systemic inflammatory response, including leukocytosis (white blood cell count: 21.3×10^9/L; 85% neutrophils) and elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 42 mm/h; C-reactive protein: 15.4 mg/dL). Risk level not explicitly stated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Patient received empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and was transitioned to valacyclovir for suspected disseminated HSV infection; leukocytosis improved rapidly with persistently sterile cultures. Subsequent serologic testing demonstrated elevated Coxsackievirus A and B titers (≥1:100), supporting an enteroviral etiology, but limitations of serologic testing preclude definitive confirmation in the absence of paired titers or lesion-based PCR. Skin biopsy demonstrated nonspecific inflammatory changes with negative direct immunofluorescence.

analysis.brief_en: A 33-year-old immunocompetent woman presented with severe vulvar ulcerations, oral ulcers, and a pustular lower-extremity rash, initially concerning for disseminated herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection or Behçet's disease. Despite extensive testing, infectious and autoimmune evaluations were unrevealing, and cultures remained sterile. The patient received empiric therapy, and leukocytosis improved. Subsequent serologic testing showed elevated Coxsackievirus A and B titers, supporting a probable enteroviral etiology, though definitive confirmation was limited by testing methodology. This rare case highlights the diagnostic challenges of atypical adult Coxsackievirus presentations, which can mimic more common conditions, and underscores the importance of considering viral etiologies to avoid unnecessary antimicrobial exposure.

analysis.time: Publication date: July 28, 2026. Event period: January 2020 to December 2025 (surveillance data). Seasonal window: August through October (late summer/early fall).
analysis.location_and_population: Affected population: Children (previously healthy, predominantly). Design population: Families with children.
analysis.event: CDC published six years of acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) surveillance data. AFM is a rare neurologic condition affecting the spinal cord's gray matter, confirmed through clinical symptoms, MRI, and laboratory testing. The report highlights a decline in cases (17-48 annually) compared to pre-2020 peaks (120-238) and notes an unexplained absence of AFM despite EV-D68 circulation in 2022, 2024, and 2025.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Cases: 17-48 annually (2020-2025), down from 120-238 in 2014, 2016, 2018. Deaths: Not reported. Exposures: Not specified. Risk: Low for individual families (fewer than 50 cases/year in ~73 million children). Surveillance gap: Only ~50% of AFM patients tested for poliovirus in stool specimens.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Investigation: Ongoing; CDC maintains AFM surveillance. Testing: Stool specimen collection recommended for all suspected AFM cases to detect potential polio. Prevention: Polio vaccination coverage (75-100% with 3+ doses) is reassuring; no specific EV-D68 vaccine. Uncertainty: Unexplained decline in AFM despite EV-D68 resurgence; no established reason for the break in biennial pattern. Source limitation: Full original article reviewed (content_status: full).

analysis.brief_en: The CDC has released six years of acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) surveillance data, revealing a significant decline in cases from pre-2020 peaks. Between 2020 and 2025, the U.S. recorded 17-48 AFM cases annually, down from 120-238 in 2014, 2016, and 2018. Notably, AFM cases remained low even when EV-D68, the virus most closely associated with AFM, circulated at elevated levels in 2022, 2024, and 2025. The report highlights a critical surveillance gap: only about half of AFM patients were tested for poliovirus in stool specimens, despite AFM being clinically indistinguishable from paralytic polio. The CDC recommends stool testing for all suspected AFM cases and emphasizes maintaining polio vaccination. The reasons for the recent decline in AFM cases remain unexplained, and officials continue to monitor the seasonal late-summer/early-fall window for potential changes in the pattern.

analysis.time: Published on July 28, 2026. The research recreated a 14-day intestinal infection period.
analysis.location_and_population: Institute of Science Tokyo (Science Tokyo). The study used a gut-on-a-chip model with human pluripotent stem cells to mimic the human intestine.
analysis.event: Scientists successfully recreated a 14-day intestinal infection caused by Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) using a gut-on-a-chip model. The virus multiplied for 14 days without damaging intestinal cells, matching clinical observations in patients.

analysis.brief_en: Scientists at the Institute of Science Tokyo have successfully recreated a 14-day intestinal infection caused by Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) using a gut-on-a-chip model. This breakthrough addresses a long-standing mystery: why patients rarely develop intestinal symptoms despite carrying the virus for weeks. The research revealed that EV-A71 multiplies in the intestines without damaging cells and evades the body's immune defenses by suppressing interferon responses. The gut-on-a-chip, developed from human pluripotent stem cells, provides a more realistic platform for testing new treatments, as conventional cell lines cannot sustain the long-term infection observed in patients. This advancement may help researchers understand how the virus spreads and develop better therapies for hand, foot and mouth disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms by which EV-A71 induces neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, as the underlying processes remain incompletely understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized human brain specimens and a mouse model to investigate EV-A71-induced BBB disruption and neuroinflammation, focusing on the role of the C5a-C5aR1 axis in regulating neutrophil migration.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed immunofluorescence analysis to examine the activation of the C5a-C5aR1 axis in fatal EV-A71 cases and generated neutrophil-specific PAD4 knockout mice to study the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in BBB injury.
analysis.main_results: Inflammatory cell infiltration in the brainstem and BBB disruption were observed following EV-A71 infection in human brain specimens and mouse models. The C5a-C5aR1 axis was robustly activated in fatal EV-A71 cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the critical role of the C5a-C5aR1-neutrophil/NETs pathway in EV-A71 encephalitis pathogenesis, offering a novel mechanism for BBB disruption and neuroinflammation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the pathogenesis of EV-A71 encephalitis and support the development of therapeutic strategies targeting the C5a-C5aR1 axis for critically ill patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on animal models and human brain specimens, which may not fully represent the complexity of human disease. However, the evidence is strong due to the direct observation of BBB disruption and the use of targeted genetic and pharmacological interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanisms by which EV-A71 induces neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption. Using human brain specimens and a mouse model, the researchers observed pronounced inflammatory cell infiltration and BBB disruption following EV-A71 infection. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed robust activation of the C5a-C5aR1 axis in fatal cases, and C5aR1 knockout mice showed reduced BBB injury. The study highlights the critical role of the C5a-C5aR1-neutrophil/NETs pathway in EV-A71 encephalitis and suggests it as a potential therapeutic target. The findings are significant for understanding the pathogenesis of EV-A71 infections and may inform future research and treatment strategies. However, the study's reliance on animal models and limited human data may affect the generalizability of the results.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus 71 (EV-A71) is a major causative agent of severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in young children. However, the molecular interplay between EV-A71 and host factors, particularly how these interactions govern viral replication, remains incompletely understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To systematically identify host factors involved in EV-A71 infection, we performed comprehensive identification of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) by mass spectrometry (ChIRP-MS) during viral infection and identified 374 host proteins associated with the EV-A71 genomic RNA.
analysis.methods: Integrative analysis of existing datasets further revealed a broader association between Matrin 3 (MATR3) and enteroviruses, which we functionally validated through gain- and loss-of-function assays, demonstrating that MATR3 acts as a proviral factor essential for efficient EV-A71 replication.
analysis.main_results: Mechanistically, we show that MATR3 specifically binds to the 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) of EV-A71 RNA via its second RNA recognition motif (RRM2).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This interaction promotes RNA-dependent condensate formation of MATR3, thereby enhancing viral RNA stability.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Furthermore, MATR3 recruits the host palmitoyltransferase ZDHHC20 to the viral ribonucleoprotein complex, facilitating MATR3 palmitoylation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This posttranslational modification promotes the assembly of a stable ribonucleoprotein complex that cooperatively stabilizes the viral genome and supports efficient replication.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms by which EV-A71 interacts with host factors to facilitate viral replication. The research highlights the role of Matrin 3 (MATR3) in stabilizing EV-A71 RNA through its RNA recognition motif (RRM2) and by recruiting the host palmitoyltransferase ZDHHC20. The findings demonstrate that MATR3 acts as a proviral factor essential for efficient EV-A71 replication, revealing a novel pathway involving RNA condensate formation and palmitoylation. The study provides a comprehensive profiling dataset of host proteins associated with EV-A71 RNA, which may inform future research on viral replication and host-virus interactions. While the study identifies a key mechanism, the evidence is based on in vitro assays and does not account for in vivo complexities, which may limit its generalizability.

analysis.research_question_and_background: In 2014, 2016, and 2018, infection with enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) was associated with outbreaks of a poliomyelitis-like paralytic syndrome, called acute flaccid myelitis (AFM).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study tested the effectiveness of a monoclonal antibody, EV68-228-N, in a mouse model of EV-D68 induced acute flaccid myelitis (AFM).
analysis.methods: The study used a mouse model of AFM and tested the monoclonal antibody EV68-228-N against both 2014 and 2016 EV-D68 isolates.
analysis.main_results: We found that EV68-228-N effectively halted the progression of paralysis when tested against both 2014 and 2016 EV-D68 isolates in an immunocompetent mouse model of AFM.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Here, we show that a monoclonal antibody, EV68-228-N, can quickly stop the progression of paralysis in a mouse model of AFM, even when treatment is initiated after the onset of paralysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This work suggests that EV68-228-N treatment has the potential to halt the progression of paralysis in AFM patients who present at the clinic with neurologic symptoms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The IC 50 of EV68-228-N against 2014 and 2016 EV-D68 isolates was confirmed in vitro to be less than 330 ng/mL, and EV68-228-N was found to be equally effective at neutralizing 2018 and 2022 viral isolates without any evidence of emerging resistance.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of the monoclonal antibody EV68-228-N to halt the progression of paralysis in a mouse model of EV-D68 induced acute flaccid myelitis (AFM). The research highlights that EV-D68 has been linked to AFM outbreaks in 2014, 2016, and 2018, and that only a small fraction of infected patients develop AFM, often seeking treatment after neurological symptoms appear. The study demonstrates that EV68-228-N effectively stops paralysis progression in mice infected with EV-D68 isolates from 2014 and 2016, even when treatment is initiated after paralysis onset. The antibody also retains neutralization potential against newer isolates, with no evidence of resistance. These findings suggest that EV68-228-N could be a promising therapeutic option for AFM patients. However, the study is limited to a mouse model, and further research is needed to confirm its efficacy in humans.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the genetic variation and recombinant characteristics of echovirus 3 (E-3) in relation to severe and mild cases of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in Guizhou Province, China, as E-3 has recently been identified as an emerging pathogen associated with both clinical outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed eight E-3 strains from severe and mild HFMD cases and examined seroprevalence in Guizhou Province using 178 samples. It focused on the molecular features of these strains and their association with clinical severity.
analysis.methods: The study employed phylogenetic analysis, recombination analysis, and seroprevalence testing to compare genetic features between E-3 strains from severe and mild HFMD cases. It also assessed replication efficiency, viral titers, and cytopathogenicity in vitro.
analysis.main_results: Eight shared nucleotide substitutions in the untranslated regions (UTRs) and six shared amino acid substitutions in the open reading frame (ORF) were identified between E-3 strains from severe and mild case groups. Additionally, 31 nucleotide substitutions were specific to the severe case group, while 41 were specific to the mild case group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that genetic variations in E-3 may contribute to differences in clinical severity, with severe case strains showing enhanced replication efficiency, higher viral titers, and increased cytopathogenicity. These results provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying E-3 pathogenicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the genetic diversity and potential for enhanced transmissibility of E-3, which could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies for HFMD in Guizhou Province and other regions with similar epidemiological patterns.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single geographic region and the use of in vitro data. However, the evidence is strong due to the detailed genetic and seroprevalence analyses, and the findings are supported by multiple observations of nucleotide and amino acid substitutions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the genetic variation and recombinant characteristics of echovirus 3 (E-3) in relation to severe and mild cases of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in Guizhou Province, China. It reports eight shared nucleotide substitutions in the untranslated regions (UTRs) and six shared amino acid substitutions in the open reading frame (ORF) between E-3 strains from severe and mild case groups. Additionally, 31 nucleotide substitutions were specific to the severe case group, while 41 were specific to the mild case group. Recombination analysis revealed complex interserotypic recombination with echovirus 21 (E-21), enterovirus B80 (EV-B80), and echovirus 30 (E-30). The severe case group strains demonstrated enhanced replication efficiency, higher viral titers, and greater cytopathogenicity in vitro, suggesting a potential link between genetic variations and clinical severity. The study also found a seropositivity rate of 52.25% and a geometric mean titer (GMT) of 1:28.23 for E-3, indicating the prevalence of asymptomatic infections. These findings provide critical insights into the molecular epidemiology of E-3 and its role in HFMD, supporting further research into its pathogenicity and evolution.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the epidemic patterns of enterovirus infections in the Far Eastern Federal District over a long-term period (2006–2024) due to the increasing incidence of enterovirus infections (EVI) in the summer-autumn period, with outbreaks occurring.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective epidemiological analysis of EVI incidence in the Far Eastern Federal District was conducted using nonparametric and parametric statistical methods. The highest incidence rates were recorded in the Ural and Far Eastern Federal Districts.
analysis.methods: The study involved a retrospective epidemiological analysis of EVI incidence in the Far Eastern Federal District, utilizing nonparametric and parametric statistical methods to examine the epidemic process.
analysis.main_results: A trend toward a moderate increase in EVI incidence with an increase in the registration of outbreaks has been identified. The incidence of herpangina and exanthemic forms has increased among the clinical manifestations of enterovirus infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the circulation of certain enterovirus genotypes, particularly Enterovirus alphacoxsackie species, has led to changes in the clinical patterns of enterovirus infections and likely affected the age distribution of infected children.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the need for anti-epidemic measures not only during the seasonal outbreaks but also during the interepidemic period to address the increasing incidence of enterovirus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a retrospective analysis, which may introduce biases and limit the ability to establish causality. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on historical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the long-term dynamics of enterovirus infections (EVI) in the Far Eastern Federal District of Russia from 2006 to 2024. It identifies a moderate increase in EVI incidence alongside more frequent outbreaks, with a notable rise in herpangina and exanthemic forms. The research suggests that the predominance of Enterovirus alphacoxsackie species since 2017 may have altered clinical patterns and age distribution of affected children. The findings emphasize the importance of implementing anti-epidemic measures beyond seasonal periods. However, the study's retrospective design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) causes severe neurological complications in pediatric hand, foot, and mouth disease, yet the structural basis of its recognition by the attachment factor P-selectin glycoprotein ligand-1 (PSGL-1) remains undefined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used cryo-electron microscopy to compare a PSGL-1–non-binding EV-A71 strain (EV-V) with a PSGL-1–binding strain (EV-R) and analyzed EV-R particles incubated with a sulfated 20-residue PSGL-1 N-terminal peptide (sPSGL-1; residues 42–61).
analysis.methods: Cryo-EM reconstructions were performed with symmetry-relaxed (C1) conditions to a 2.38 Å resolution, focusing on the fivefold vertex of EV-R particles to detect low-occupancy densities and localized structural changes associated with sPSGL-1 incubation.
analysis.main_results: A VP1-145 substitution in EV-R disrupts the interprotomer E145–K244 interaction, repositions K244, and increases local electrostatic potential at the fivefold vertex, with vertex-adjacent densities consistent with an aromatic ring near VP1 K244 and localized structural differences in VP1 loops.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that sulfated PSGL-1 primes the EV-A71 fivefold vertex through electrostatic interactions, inducing localized structural remodeling that facilitates early-stage receptor recognition without triggering global uncoating, representing a newly defined mechanism of receptor engagement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This structural insight into EV-A71–PSGL-1 interactions may inform the design of antiviral strategies targeting receptor binding or capsid priming, potentially improving surveillance and therapeutic approaches for severe EV-A71 infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study analyzed a compact/closed particle population and did not observe uncoating-associated A-particle transitions, limiting conclusions about later-stage receptor-mediated entry events; the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of functional validation beyond structural observations.

analysis.summary_en: This study resolves how sulfated PSGL-1 primes the EV-A71 capsid for receptor engagement by inducing localized structural remodeling at the fivefold vertex. Using cryo-EM, the authors show that a VP1-145 substitution in a PSGL-1–binding strain (EV-R) disrupts interprotomer interactions, increases local electrostatic potential, and creates a lysine-rich cleft that accommodates sPSGL-1 without triggering global uncoating. The work defines a new mechanism of early-stage receptor recognition for EV-A71, highlighting potential targets for antiviral design while acknowledging that later entry stages and functional consequences remain unexamined.

analysis.research_question_and_background: EV-A71 and EV-D68 are recognized causes of severe neurological complications such as acute flaccid myelitis, yet the molecular mechanisms driving neurovirulence and neuromuscular impairment remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neuromuscular organoids to model infection by EV-A71 and EV-D68 in a human-relevant system.
analysis.methods: Viral infection was performed on neuromuscular organoids, followed by transcriptomic profiling to assess gene network changes and protein-level analyses of synaptic and apoptotic markers.
analysis.main_results: Both viruses infected neuronal populations within organoids, with EV-A71 showing higher replication levels; transcriptomic analysis revealed downregulation of neuronal and muscular gene networks, and both viruses were associated with increased cleaved caspase-3 and sporadic cleavage of SNAP25.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate virus-specific downstream effects on neuronal and muscle pathways and demonstrate that neuromuscular organoids provide a robust platform for dissecting enterovirus–host interactions relevant to acute flaccid myelitis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides mechanistic insights into EV-A71 and EV-D68 neurotropism and neuromuscular impairment, informing future surveillance and therapeutic strategies for enterovirus-associated neurological disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its in vitro organoid model and lack of in vivo validation, which constrains generalizability; however, the human-relevant system and multi-omic approach strengthen the evidence base.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the pathogenic mechanisms of enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) and enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) using human neuromuscular organoids to model infection in a human-relevant context. Both viruses infected neuronal populations, with EV-A71 exhibiting higher replication. Transcriptomic profiling showed downregulation of neuronal and muscular gene networks, while protein analyses revealed increased cleaved caspase-3 and sporadic cleavage of the synaptic protein SNAP25, indicating activation of apoptotic signaling. EV-A71 preferentially suppressed neuronal pathways, whereas both viruses comparably affected muscle-associated gene expression. The authors conclude that these virus-specific downstream effects validate neuromuscular organoids as a robust platform for dissecting enterovirus–host interactions relevant to acute flaccid myelitis. The findings highlight mechanistic differences between EV-A71 and EV-D68 and suggest potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop potent inhibitors of coronaviral and enteroviral proteases by leveraging structural insights from co-crystal complexes. Viral proteases represent validated targets for direct-acting antivirals and the treatment of associated infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the synthesis of two macrocyclic series and their characterization through co-crystal structures of M pro of SARS-CoV-2 and the 3C pro of enterovirus D68. The research focused on human enteroviruses, particularly EV-A71, EV-D68, and CVB3.
analysis.methods: To enhance molecular rigidity, the proximal residues were conformationally fixed by macrocyclization. The study reported the synthesis of two macrocyclic series, i.e., exocyclic nitriles with linked P3 and P1 residues and endocyclic α-ketoamides with linked P1’ and P2 residues, and characterized their binding modes and bioactivities.
analysis.main_results: The 17-membered macrocyclic α-ketoamide 20 f inhibited M pro (IC50 = 370 nM) and exerted anti-SARS-CoV-2 effects (EC50 = 1.9 μM). Notably, 20 f exhibited very potent antiviral activities with EC50’s of 33, 133, and 146 nM against EV-D68, EV-A71, and CVB3, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates how broad-spectrum activity can be achieved with direct-acting antivirals by designing inhibitors that target multiple viral proteases, including those of coronaviruses and enteroviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a foundation for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral drugs that could be used to treat infections caused by human enteroviruses and coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on structural and biochemical data without clinical trials, and the evidence is moderate as it relies on in vitro and in silico results rather than in vivo or clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the development of potent inhibitors for coronaviral and enteroviral proteases through structure-based macrocyclization of α-ketoamides. The researchers observed spatial proximity of sidechains in co-crystal structures of SARS-CoV-2's M pro and enterovirus D68's 3C pro, leading to the synthesis of two macrocyclic series. The 17-membered macrocyclic α-ketoamide 20 f showed significant inhibition of M pro and anti-SARS-CoV-2 effects, with potent antiviral activities against EV-D68, EV-A71, and CVB3. The study highlights the potential of broad-spectrum antivirals targeting multiple viral proteases. However, the findings are based on in vitro and in silico data, limiting their clinical applicability. The results suggest a novel approach to designing antivirals that could inform future research and development for treating enterovirus and coronavirus infections.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify the downstream effectors of the MAPK pathway that mediate the pro-viral function during enterovirus 71 (EV71) infection, as this remains poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the role of the MAPK-EGR1 signaling axis in EV71 replication using conventional cell lines and human colonic organoid infection models.
analysis.methods: The researchers used calycosin (CA) to target the MAPK-EGR1 axis and assessed its effects on EV71-induced expression and phosphorylation of ERK, p38, and JNK, as well as EGR1 upregulation.
analysis.main_results: Calycosin suppresses EV71-induced expression and phosphorylation of ERK, p38, and JNK, as well as the subsequent upregulation of EGR1, thereby inhibiting both viral replication and virus-induced cell death.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that the MAPK-EGR1 axis is a key host-dependent mechanism for EV71 replication and that calycosin can effectively target this axis to inhibit the virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide a mechanistic basis for developing host-directed antiviral strategies against EV71 and other enteroviruses, which could inform future therapeutic and diagnostic approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and human colonic organoid models, and the evidence is strong as it directly links CA to the inhibition of EV71 replication through the MAPK-EGR1 axis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the MAPK-EGR1 signaling axis in promoting enterovirus 71 (EV71) replication and virus-induced cell death. The researchers demonstrate that calycosin (CA), a natural isoflavone, suppresses EV71-induced expression and phosphorylation of ERK, p38, and JNK, as well as the subsequent upregulation of EGR1, thereby inhibiting both viral replication and cell death in conventional cell lines and human colonic organoid models. The findings establish the MAPK-EGR1 axis as a critical host-dependent pathway for EV71 and other enteroviruses, suggesting CA as a potential chemical probe for antiviral strategies. The study's results are supported by direct experimental evidence, but its in vitro focus limits the generalizability of the findings to in vivo settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pediatric meningitis remains a major diagnostic and therapeutic emergency because clinical presentation may be nonspecific and early etiological distinction directly influences treatment, infection control, and epidemiological surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective single-center analysis was performed using microbiological data from suspected meningitis episodes investigated between 2023 and 2025 at the “Louis Țurcanu” Emergency Hospital for Children, Timișoara.
analysis.methods: The distribution of suspected and confirmed episodes, annual etiological patterns, age-group differences, sex-associated variation, and identified pathogens were assessed using descriptive statistics and trend analysis.
analysis.main_results: Among 641 suspected episodes, 58 were microbiologically confirmed, corresponding to an overall positivity rate of 9.05%. Viral meningitis was the most frequent etiology, accounting for 30 episodes (51.72%), followed by bacterial meningitis with 22 episodes (37.93%) and fungal meningitis with 6 episodes (10.34%). Etiological distribution changed significantly over the study period: viral episodes increased from 22.22% in 2023 to 77.78% in 2025, while bacterial episodes decreased from 66.67% to 22.22%. Viral meningitis predominated in children aged 1–6 years and was more frequent among male patients, whereas bacterial meningitis remained more frequent in infants. Enterovirus became the dominant identified agent in 2025.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The local epidemiology of confirmed pediatric meningitis showed an observed redistribution among confirmed episodes toward viral etiologies, particularly enteroviral meningitis, alongside a proportional decline in bacterial episodes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support continued etiological surveillance and the integration of rapid molecular testing with conventional microbiology in the diagnostic management of suspected pediatric meningitis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design and retrospective nature, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is moderate as it is based on descriptive statistics and trend analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the changing etiological patterns of pediatric meningitis over three years at a tertiary pediatric emergency hospital in Romania. It found that viral meningitis, particularly enteroviral meningitis, became more prevalent, increasing from 22.22% in 2023 to 77.78% in 2025, while bacterial meningitis decreased proportionally. analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The suspected case rate reached 36.1 per 1,000 outpatients in the 30th week, a 33-fold increase from the 1.1 recorded in the 19th week. The disease is highly contagious and spreads through contaminated water, feces, or secretions. No specific treatment is available, and prevention relies on personal hygiene measures.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Health authorities have issued prevention guidelines, emphasizing handwashing and cleaning frequently touched items. Patients are advised to avoid public facilities until blisters heal. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency is conducting sentinel surveillance, and the situation is under active monitoring.

analysis.brief_en: A recent report from Seoul Economic Daily highlights a significant surge in hand, foot, and mouth disease cases among children in Korea during the summer of 2026. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency noted a 33-fold increase in suspected cases over the past 12 weeks, with the rate reaching 36.1 per 1,000 outpatients in the 30th week of the year (July 19–25). Among children aged 0 to 6, the suspected case rate was even higher at 48.3 per 1,000. The disease, primarily caused by coxsackievirus A16 and enterovirus A71, spreads through contaminated water, feces, or secretions, and is highly contagious. Health authorities have urged caution, emphasizing the importance of personal hygiene measures such as frequent handwashing and cleaning toys and doorknobs. Patients are advised to avoid public facilities until their blisters heal, and isolation guidelines are recommended for water playgrounds and swimming pools. While there is no specific treatment, the disease typically resolves on its own within three to seven days. The report underscores the need for vigilance in preventing the spread of the virus, especially in communal settings where children gather.

analysis.scope_and_question: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a re-emerging pathogen associated with severe acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) and pneumonia, predominantly in children but also capable of causing severe disease in immunocompromised adults. Seroprevalence data are essential for understanding population immunity, age-specific susceptibility, and viral transmission dynamics; yet, such data for the period after the COVID-19 pandemic are scarce.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We conducted a cross-sectional serological survey to characterize the neutralizing antibody profile of EV-D68 among children in Xiamen, China, in 2022. A total of 453 children aged 0–16 years (217 with acute respiratory tract infection [ARTI] and 236 without) were enrolled. Neutralizing antibody (NtAb) titers against the EV-D68 STL strain were measured using a microneutralization assay, seropositivity was defined as a titer ≥1:16. Multivariable regression and analysis of covariance were used to adjust for age and sex.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Overall seroprevalence was 96.0% (435/453), exceeding 90.0% in every age subgroup (0–1 y: 100%; 1–3 y: 97.6%; 3–5 y: 92.6%; ≥5 y: 96.2%). The geometric mean titer (GMT) was 76.78 (95% CI: 68.32–85.24).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: After adjustment, ARTI status was not significantly associated with seropositivity (adjusted OR = 1.42, 95% CI: 0.46–4.41, p = 0.542). In an exploratory comparison, children with ARTI showed nominally higher antibody titers than those without (Mann–Whitney U test, p = 0.003), although the absence of EV-D68-specific PCR testing precludes etiologic attribution of respiratory symptoms to EV-D68 infection.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings provide key reference data for ongoing serosurveillance, outbreak risk assessment, and the evaluation of future vaccines or immunoprophylactic strategies should they become available.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional serological study conducted in Xiamen, China, in 2022 aimed to characterize the neutralizing antibody profile of Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) among children. The study enrolled 453 children aged 0–16 years, with 217 having acute respiratory tract infection (ARTI) and 236 without. Overall seroprevalence was 96.0%, with all age subgroups showing seroprevalence above 90.0%. The geometric mean titer (GMT) was 76.78 (95% CI: 68.32–85.24). Although children with ARTI showed nominally higher antibody titers, the lack of EV-D68-specific PCR testing prevented etiologic attribution. The findings offer critical data for serosurveillance, outbreak risk assessment, and future vaccine development.
